critical_code_review_comments: server.py assistant_chat: FRASBERG_KEY_ROUTES has no 'chat' key, so key_order('chat') iterates all 8 keys sequentially. With upstream currently in turbulence this means each client wait is ~15-25s. Consider short-circuiting after N=2 keys for chat (or add 'chat:<prefix>' to KEY_ROUTES) to reduce user-visible latency on the floating widget.

server.py assistant_chat parses the SSE stream with a regex over r.text; if the upstream later streams genuinely (chunked), buffering the full body before parsing can delay first-token UX. Consider httpx streaming + incremental parse once Frasberg chat is stable.

AssistantChat.jsx: the loader is rendered inside the message list but not scrolled into view, and there's no auto-scroll to bottom when new messages arrive. On long conversations the user won't see new bubbles. Add a ref + scrollIntoView on msgs change.

AssistantChat.jsx: the error bubble text is the raw backend detail. For the turbulence case ('Luchii Chat (Frasberg) is replying with a turbulence error') it's acceptable, but a generic HTTP error from upstream could leak internal phrasing to end users. Consider mapping 5xx details to a friendly message with a Retry button.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Assistant chat regression lives in /app/backend/tests/test_assistant_chat.py. The 503-turbulence assertion is tied to the current Frasberg upstream state; once Frasberg luchii-6-plus starts replying normally that test will flip to expecting 200 with {reply, session_id, engine:'luchii-6-plus'} — update test_chat_returns_503_turbulence accordingly. Do NOT pip install requirements-gpu.txt in /root/.venv and do NOT trigger heavy image/video/3d/music jobs on this CPU pod.
